description: RAPID: A Coordinated Structural Engineering Response to Hurricane Irma (in Florida) is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Tracy Kijewski-Correa, University of Notre Dame (nd.edu). Hurricane Irma left a path of considerable destruction across the Caribbean, eventually making its first landfall in the continental US at Cudjoe Key in southern Florida on September 10, 2017, with Category 4 winds reaching 58 m/s (130 mph). Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/DS2TX0C. Keywords: Hurricane Irma, Florida, Wind, Surge, Reconissance. Published 2018-06-19. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated in the DesignSafe listing (publication licences offered are CC BY 4.0, ODC-By, CC0 and GPL; project page not read). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
